mechanism_claims.claim_text: Trp2/Phe5 and the C-terminal helix support rapid gram-negative membrane permeabilization; papiliocin kills E. coli faster than W2A/F5A analogs and PapN series peptides do not detectably kill within one hour at 4x MIC.
direct_assay_types: time-kill kinetics in E. coli KCTC 1682
mechanism_claims.limitations: Time-kill kinetics supports bactericidal timing; exact curve values beyond stated text are not digitized from the figure.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: Calcein leakage, membrane depolarization, and NPN uptake assays support membrane-permeabilizing activity, with Trp2 more important than Phe5 for E. coli membrane effects.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Model membrane and fluorescence assays support membrane interaction; figure-only exact dose-response points are not over-extracted.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: STD-NMR and FITC-LPS experiments support interaction of the N-terminal aromatic residues with LPS and LPS aggregate disaggregation by papiliocin/PapN analogs.

mechanism_claims.limitations: LPS binding/disaggregation supports anti-inflammatory mechanism context but does not by itself quantify antimicrobial potency.
